title: What holds the shape?
hook: Two different silhouettes can share a structural trait.

doesNotKnow: What material makes up much of the internal skeleton in both sharks and rays?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: What material makes up much of the internal skeleton in both sharks and rays?

claims.text: What material makes up much of the internal skeleton in both sharks and rays? The two panels highlight an internal skeleton in a shark and a ray. Both belong to cartilaginous fishes: much of their skeletal support is cartilage rather than the bony skeleton typical of many other fishes. The shapes are simplified.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, vertebrates, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A ray has a skeleton made largely of cartilage. Which other animal in this comparison shares that trait? Sharks and rays are cartilaginous fishes.
